bullets: Last game of the video (video time 1364.5-1500.0, clock 2:48 down to 0:35), the same single deck used all session. The per-game HUD read swapped Goblin Barrel for Tornado; that is a misread — Goblin Barrel is named six times and cast three times here, while every 'NATO'/Tornado reference is Ryley describing the opponent's card.

The deck is piloted as chip-plus-activation, not as a push deck: Wall Breakers and Goblin Barrel go in as a pair on the opponent's tower (t=1441-1445, t=1477.5 — "We do have the nice evo barrel wall breakers push here"), while Tesla, Royal Delivery, Skeletons, Fire Spirit and Magic Archer stay entirely on his own half.

Its signature play in this game is using cheap defence to activate his own King Tower: Skeletons to pull the Bowler and a Fire Spirit to retarget it at clock 2:27-2:23, failing to a Freeze ("Great freeze by him to prevent the activation", t=1401), then Ronin at the bridge plus a late Tesla at clock 1:20-1:08 which succeeds ("Nice king activation... the golden knight's literally dead", t=1469-1471).

Ronin is the deck's tempo card rather than its tank — both uses (t=1418.8, t=1458.3) exist to force a defensive spend: "forcing him to have to defend the Ronin and then he just wasn't able to prevent the king activation" (t=1484-1488). The game ends with the enemy left tower at 265 HP and Ryley reading out the video's outro over it.

new_deck.display_name: Ronin Goblin Barrel Wall Breakers Ryley
new_deck.rationale: Goblin Barrel, Wall Breakers, Skeletons and Fire Spirit all bait the same small spells, and at a 2.875 average cost the deck cycles back to them faster than the opponent can hold an answer.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: Two cheap chip threats — Goblin Barrel and Wall Breakers — are played as a pair, so a single small spell or swarm can never cover both, and the deck cycles back to them almost immediately. Everything else is defence bought at one to four elixir (Skeletons, Fire Spirit, Royal Delivery, Tesla, Magic Archer), which lets Ryley answer a Graveyard control deck's Bowler, Zappies and Graveyard without ever spending his win conditions on defence. The Ronin is the tempo lever: dropped at the bridge it forces a defensive commitment, and while the opponent is paying for it the defensive building can be placed late enough to also drag Ryley's King Tower into the fight — "If I Ronin at the bridge, isn't this just a guaranteed activation?" (t=1455). Against Tornado decks the same cheapness lets him place the barrel off-centre and still threaten, because he can afford to throw it again next cycle.
